findings.title: Stable Channel Update for Desktop
findings.summary_md: Google promoted Chrome 158 to the Stable channel for Windows, Mac and Linux, with 158.0.8127.36 on Linux and 158.0.8127.36/.37 on Windows and Mac rolling out over the coming days and weeks. The advisory lists 204 security fixes and six Critical CVEs: CVE-2026-130963 (use after free in WebView), CVE-2026-131031 and CVE-2026-131054 (out of bounds writes in GPU and ANGLE), CVE-2026-131060 (buffer overflow in Media), CVE-2026-131008 (use after free in GarbageCollection) and CVE-2026-130975 (use after free in WebAudio). Google notes that bug details and links may stay restricted until a majority of users are updated.

findings.title: Chrome for Android Update
findings.summary_md: Google released Chrome 158.0.8127.42 for Android, with availability on Google Play over the next few days. The post describes stability and performance improvements and says Android releases carry the same security fixes as the corresponding desktop releases, 158.0.8127.36/.37 on Windows and Mac and 158.0.8127.36 on Linux, unless otherwise noted.

findings.title: CVE-2026-130963 Detail
findings.summary_md: NVD published the Google-reported record for CVE-2026-130963 on November 17, 2026, with CWE-416, Chromium severity Critical and status Awaiting Analysis. Its description says a use after free in WebView in Google Chrome on Android before 158.0.8127.36 let a remote attacker execute arbitrary code outside the sandbox via crafted network traffic. The record references the Chrome 158 stable advisory and Chromium issue 562000561.
